findings.title: Stored XSS: untrusted RSS content stored with raw_html cook_method
findings.body: poll_feed reads `i.content` from the feed, runs only `CGI.unescapeHTML(...scrub)` (which strips invalid bytes but does not sanitize HTML), and passes it straight into `TopicEmbed.import`. import then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and, because Post#cook returns `raw` for that mode and best.html.erb renders the post with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, any `<script>` (or other active) tags in the feed end up executing inside an iframe whose origin is Discourse. The same vector exists for TopicEmbed.import_remote (Readability output is trusted and the raw URL body for Disqus) and the disqus.thor import. Anyone with admin control of feed_polling_url (or embeddable_host, or a Disqus import file) can get script execution in Discourse's origin and read cookies / take actions on behalf of logged-in users visiting the embed iframe. The fix is to never assign raw_html to imported posts from external sources; run them through the normal cook/sanitize pipeline.

findings.title: New cook_method column default of 1 likely marks every existing post as raw_html
findings.body: The migration adds `cook_method integer default 1 not null` to posts. Post.cook_methods is `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)` and Post#cook short-circuits to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. With conventional (0-indexed) Enum implementations `[:regular] == 0` and `[:raw_html] == 1`, so existing rows default to raw_html, which means Post#cook now returns the unprocessed markdown source. The before_save hook does `self.cooked = cook(raw, topic_id: topic_id) unless new_record?`, so the next edit on any existing post will overwrite `cooked` with raw markdown and visibly break rendering across the entire site. The migration default should be whichever value Enum maps to `:regular` (verify the Enum implementation; it is almost certainly 0, not 1).

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring match, allowing spoofed origins
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any event whose origin contains `discourseUrl` as a substring. Anything like `https://attacker.com/?x=https://discourse.host`, or any subdomain/hostname that embeds the literal, passes the check, and the parent's height (or anything else e.data ever carries) can be set by an attacker frame. Because this same message handler also reads any e.data.type, a malicious frame could trigger other branches later. Use `new URL(discourseUrl).origin` (with a trailing slash check) and compare exactly: `new URL(e.origin).origin === expectedOrigin`.

findings.title: embed/best does not validate that embed_url belongs to the embeddable host
findings.body: `embed_url = params.require(:embed_url)` is used directly in `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` and passed to `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, embed_url: embed_url)` without verifying its host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. The host check happens only asynchronously inside TopicRetriever. Anyone who knows an existing embed_url can render that topic via `/embed/best`, and any caller can enqueue a retrieve for a non-matching URL (it just silently no-ops in the retriever, but still hits the DB, the queue, and reveals embed existence). Validate the host synchronously in the controller before doing the lookup or enqueueing.

findings.title: Imported posts created with skip_validations: true and raw_html can persist arbitrary content with no Sanitize pass
findings.body: When `TopicEmbed.import` creates the initial post it passes `skip_validations: true` along with `cook_method: raw_html`. Combined, the post's `cooked` field stores whatever HTML the caller supplied, including `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>`, javascript: links, etc., and Post#cook then returns that raw content unmolested. Even though `absolutize_urls` runs on the content, it does not sanitize. Two follow-up problems: (1) the Disqus thor path later creates further reply posts via PostCreator without setting `cook_method`, mixing modes in the same topic; (2) `revisor.revise!(... , skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` overwrites the post with whatever the next import produces, also bypassed. Sanitize imported HTML before storing it and do not pair `skip_validations` with raw_html.

findings.title: Synchronously executes the scheduled PollFeed job on every retrieve
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` does `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inside the retriever job's execution. This pulls and parses the full RSS feed, hits RSS hosts, and writes TopicEmbeds for every item in the feed, all while the retriever itself (triggered by a user GET to /embed/best) is queued behind it. A large feed will make every embed request stall, and it ignores the PollFeed scheduling/throttling guarantees. The retrieve should only try to import the single embed_url, not rerun the whole feed poller inline.
